source_text: In Sudanese communities, particularly in the northern regions, female genital mutilation (FGM) is primarily justified as a means to control female sexuality and ensure premarital chastity, with families and practitioners believing it curbs perceived excessive sexual desire and promotes fidelity within marriage.
